question: Got reject 22 on a Victoza claim, what now?
assumption: NY Medicaid / NYRx claim, because the question is a coverage/billing reject and no other program was named.
answer:
Assuming NY Medicaid: reject **22** on **Victoza** is the BLTG DAW edit. **Victoza® is preferred** on the current NYRx PDL dated **9/14/2026** and flagged **BLTG**; **liraglutide (gen Victoza®) is non-preferred**.

1. Bill **brand Victoza®** with **DAW 9**. Other DAW codes trigger reject 22; exception: **DAW 1** if the Rx says **Brand Medically Necessary**.
2. BLTG brands do **not** require DAW/“Brand Medically Necessary,” have a **generic copay**, and the list is subject to change.
3. If PA also hits, GLP-1 criteria require a covered FDA/compendia-supported indication; PA is required with concurrent GLP-1 + DPP-IV use. PA must be requested by the prescriber/authorized agent; pharmacist may obtain up to a **72-hour emergency supply** PA if unable to reach prescriber.

NYRx Preferred Drug Program (PDP) Preferred Drug List > NYS Medicaid NYRx Brand Less Than Generic (BLTG) Program
[p 77]
On April 26, 2010, NYRx, the Medicaid Pharmacy Program, implemented a new cost-containment initiative, which promotes the use of certain multisource brand name drugs when the cost of the brand name drug is less expensive than the generic equivalent.
In conformance with State Education Law, which intends that patients receive the lower cost alternative, brand name drugs included in this program:
Do not require "Dispense as Written" (DAW) or "Brand Medically Necessary" on the prescription
Have a generic copayment
Are paid at the Brand Name Drug reimbursement rate or usual and customary price, whichever is lower (SMAC/FUL are not applied)
Do not require a new prescription if the drug is removed from this program
Bosulif ® tablet, Janumet ® , Januvia ® , and Xyrem ® will be added to the program
Farxiga ® and Ravicti ® will be removed from the program

ny_medicaid_pharmacy_policy (NY Medicaid, binding, 2026-09)
NYRx Pharmacy Manual Policy Guidelines (Version 2026-3) > 1.0 General Pharmacy Policy > Prior Authorization Programs
[p 15]
The Medicaid program requires prior authorization (PA) for certain drugs under the following programs:
Preferred Drug Program (PDP)
Brand When Less Than Generic Program (BLTG)
Dose Optimization Initiative
Clinical Drug Review Program (CDRP)
Drug Utilization Review (DUR) Program
Mandatory Generic Drug Program (MGDP)
Prescribers may need to obtain prior authorizations for certain drugs. Only prescribers or their authorized agent may submit a request for prior authorization. Third party requests are prohibited: prescribers may not contract with or assign authority to dispensing pharmacists, manufacturers, or other persons or companies to initiate their PA requests. General information on the prescription drug prior authorizations, including the above programs, can be found at the following website: https://newyork.fhsc.com.
Note: If a prior authorization number has not been obtained by the prescriber and the pharmacist is unable to reach the prescriber, the pharmacist may obtain a prior authorization for up to a 72-hour emergency supply for any drug that requires prior authorization, subject to state laws and Medicaid restrictions. The pharmacist is expected to follow up with the prescriber to determine future needs.
Pharmacy Program information is available on the Medicaid Pharmacy Program website at: https://www.health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/program/pharmacy.htm.

[p 77]
On April 26, 2010, NYRx, the Medicaid Pharmacy Program, implemented a new cost-containment initiative, which promotes the use of certain multisource brand name drugs when the cost of the brand name drug is less expensive than the generic equivalent.
In conformance with State Education Law, which intends that patients receive the lower cost alternative, brand name drugs included in this program:
Do not require "Dispense as Written" (DAW) or "Brand Medically Necessary" on the prescription
Have a generic copayment
Are paid at the Brand Name Drug reimbursement rate or usual and customary price, whichever is lower (SMAC/FUL are not applied)
Do not require a new prescription if the drug is removed from this program
Bosulif ® tablet, Janumet ® , Januvia ® , and Xyrem ® will be added to the program
Farxiga ® and Ravicti ® will be removed from the program

ny_medicaid_pharmacy_policy (NY Medicaid, binding, 2026-09)
NYRx Pharmacy Manual Policy Guidelines (Version 2026-3) > 1.0 General Pharmacy Policy > Prior Authorization Programs
[p 15]
The Medicaid program requires prior authorization (PA) for certain drugs under the following programs:
Preferred Drug Program (PDP)
Brand When Less Than Generic Program (BLTG)
Dose Optimization Initiative
Clinical Drug Review Program (CDRP)
Drug Utilization Review (DUR) Program
Mandatory Generic Drug Program (MGDP)
Prescribers may need to obtain prior authorizations for certain drugs. Only prescribers or their authorized agent may submit a request for prior authorization. Third party requests are prohibited: prescribers may not contract with or assign authority to dispensing pharmacists, manufacturers, or other persons or companies to initiate their PA requests. General information on the prescription drug prior authorizations, including the above programs, can be found at the following website: https://newyork.fhsc.com.
Note: If a prior authorization number has not been obtained by the prescriber and the pharmacist is unable to reach the prescriber, the pharmacist may obtain a prior authorization for up to a 72-hour emergency supply for any drug that requires prior authorization, subject to state laws and Medicaid restrictions. The pharmacist is expected to follow up with the prescriber to determine future needs.
Pharmacy Program information is available on the Medicaid Pharmacy Program website at: https://www.health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/program/pharmacy.htm.
